items.title: Claude Haiku 5.5 resets model pricing
items.oneliner: Anthropic cut Haiku 5.5 to $0.10 per million input tokens, forcing every inference budget spreadsheet to change.

items.title: StepFun ships a million-context MoE
items.oneliner: Step 5 Preview brings 1M context with 27B active parameters, making long-repo and document agents more practical.

items.title: Whistle makes on-device speech actually usable
items.oneliner: Whistle fits speech recognition into 16.9 MB and emits first tokens in 11 ms, which is mobile-grade latency.

items.title: OpenAI withdrew three math results
items.oneliner: OpenAI pulled three mathematical claims, a sharp reminder that AI-generated research still needs old-fashioned verification.

items.title: ChatGPT for teens faces a safety rebuke
items.oneliner: Common Sense Media called ChatGPT for Teens an unacceptable risk after self-harm alerts reportedly failed during testing.

items.title: Two AIs cracked old Enigma messages
items.oneliner: GPT-6 Astra and Opus reportedly solved unsolved Enigma traffic by building tools first, not just answering prompts.

items.title: OpenAI revenue expectations just got cut
items.oneliner: OpenAI's annualized revenue outlook dropped by $20 billion, signaling the AI market is maturing faster than hype suggested.

items.title: Samsung pushes LLMs below one bit
items.oneliner: LittleBit compresses LLM weights into the sub-1-bit regime, which could move serious models onto much cheaper hardware.

items.title: AI SRE agents finally get a benchmark
items.oneliner: Project Arena gives Kubernetes SRE agents a shared incident benchmark, which is exactly what this noisy category lacked.

items.title: Kubernetes gets a clickable terminal UI
items.oneliner: K10s wraps Kubernetes in a point-and-click TUI with context-aware AI, lowering the kubectl tax for real teams.
